claims.claim: In the committed backtest report reports/verify-2026-06-25.json, 13 of the 20 recommended repositories had gained at least 10% more stars since the day they were recommended. The report used a 7-day report filter, but every entry was observed one day after discovery (days_since_discovery: 1), so the measured growth horizon is roughly one day.
claims.metric: share of recommended repositories whose star count grew by at least 10% within the backtest window, at a score threshold of 90
claims.method: scripts/verify_scoring.py reads the committed daily reports in data/discovery-*.json, takes stars_at_discovery from them, compares against the repository's current star count, and counts a repository as taking off at growth_rate >= 0.1. claims.claim: The 100-point allocation published in README.md (the "Smart Scoring (100 points)" table and the ASCII pipeline diagram) is the constants in scripts/config.py: acceleration 40, quality 30, anti-spam 30 — 100 in total — plus a +20 deep code-quality bonus that is scaled into the quality dimension, applied to the top DEEP_CHECK_TOP_K = 20 coarse-ranked candidates.
claims.value: 40 / 30 / 30 = 100 points; +20 code-quality bonus; deep check on 20
claims.metric: maximum points per scoring dimension and the number of candidates that get the expensive deep checks
claims.method: the check ast-parses scripts/config.py and prints ACCELERATION_MAX, QUALITY_MAX, ANTISPAM_MAX, QUALITY_BONUS_MAX and DEEP_CHECK_TOP_K from the source, so changing a weight fails it without any README edit.

claims.claim: The anti-spam dimension starts at 30 points and deducts for the patterns the README lists as "Starts at 30 and deducts": a star/fork ratio above 50, an age under 3 days with more than 5000 stars, marketing buzzwords, and gaming-trainer or random-username patterns. README publishes the starting score and the thresholds; the per-rule amounts below (−10, −15, −10, −5) are the return values of scripts/anti_spam.py.
claims.value: start 30; ratio > 50 → −10; age < 3 days & 5000+ stars → −15; marketing words → −10; trainer pattern → −10; random username → −5
claims.metric: starting anti-spam score and the deduction each rule returns at its threshold boundary
claims.method: the check calls the committed scripts/anti_spam.py functions with boundary inputs (ratio 50 vs 51, 5000 vs 5001 stars) and prints what the code returns; the thresholds and effects come from the source, so a rule change fails it.

check.cmd: python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import anti_spam as a;print('start:',a.calculate_antiscore({}),'| ratio>50:',a.check_star_fork_ratio({'stars':51,'forks':1}),'(ratio=50:',str(a.check_star_fork_ratio({'stars':50,'forks':1}))+') | age<3 & stars>5000:',a.check_sudden_stars({'age_days':2,'stars':5001}),'(5000:',str(a.check_sudden_stars({'age_days':2,'stars':5000}))+') | marketing>=3:',a.check_marketing_words({'description':'best ultimate revolutionary tool'}),'| trainer:',a.check_suspicious_pattern({'full_name':'o/aimbot','description':''}),'| random-username:',a.check_suspicious_pattern({'full_name':'abc12345678/x','description':''}))"

claims.claim: Every repo recommended in the last 14 days is on the watch list or already has follow-up observations — the mechanism that makes a breakout label computable later cannot silently stop covering new discoveries.
claims.metric: recommendations in the newest discovery files vs data/watchlist.json and watch_series.json
claims.method: scripts/watchlist.py adds each recommended repo with a 14-day window and is pruned when the window closes; the check re-derives the recent discovery set from the committed daily files and requires each repo to be either still watched or already observed after its discovery date

check.cmd:
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, pathlib, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import watchlist

wl = json.loads(pathlib.Path("data/watchlist.json").read_text())["repos"]
p = pathlib.Path("data/watch_series.json")
ser = json.loads(p.read_text())["repos"] if p.exists() else {}
found = watchlist.discoveries()
floor = watchlist._window_end(watchlist._today(), -14)
recent = {n: d for n, d in found.items() if d >= floor}
bad = [n for n, d in recent.items()
       if n not in wl and not any(pt["date"] > d for pt in ser.get(n, []))]
print("watchlist", len(wl), "recent discoveries", len(recent), "uncovered", bad[:3])
assert wl, "watch list is empty"
assert recent and not bad
PY

claims.claim: The follow-up mechanism is live: the watch list is non-empty, and every record in the watch series is complete, dated no later than today, and unique per day.
claims.value: all records complete, one per day
claims.method: scripts/watchlist.record writes a fixed field set and replaces the same day's point on a rerun; the check validates every record and rejects duplicate or future dates
